messages:
jonah: Heads up — noticed steady KV residency growth on several us-west nodes for tenant `alpha-payments` when serving long-context sessions. Resident pages climb ~25% over a 30m window, eviction rate spikes, and p50 token latency drifts 120ms -> 210ms. heatmap + pprof attached in thread.
ingrid: Can you paste the heatmap output inline? also any infra changes last night (kernel selection / batching) that could affect page churn?
jonah: Paste of the condensed heatmap (rows=time buckets, cols=page age):
```
00:00 | ░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░  (low)
00:10 | ░░░░░░▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒░░░  (mid)
00:20 | ░░▒▒▒▒▒██████████▒░  (hot)
00:30 | ░░░▒███████████████  (very hot)
```
And a short extract from pprof:
```
kv_residency_ratio=0.78
kv_evictions_total=432
kv_eviction_rate=12/s
avg_kv_reuse=0.14
pagewalks_per_tick=34
```
Last deploy-bot: `canary/runtime-v3.8.1` landed @ 2198758000 with a minor kernel selection tweak (prefer fast_attention kernels for small heads). That landed ~1h before the spike.
alex_m: Quick note: the kernel change should not modify KV lifecycle, but batching heuristics were adjusted to be slightly more aggressive for 64-token requests. That can increase prefix reuse variance and increase KV churn for longctx tenants.
matthew: Idea: tenant `alpha-payments` seems to have long lived KV pages with low reuse_count; eviction scoring currently uses LRU + size. Propose weighting by reuse_count and last_access_age: score = size * (1 + lambda * reuse_penalty) * sqrt(age). Might demote large, rarely reused pages.
priya_r: +1. Also we should add a per-tenant soft watermark to limit growth: soft_quota = min(global_shard_limit * tenant_weight, base+alpha * recent_rss). When breached, favor compact eviction and background compaction.
ingrid: Can we reproduce quickly in staging? I can run a synthetic workload that mimics long-context streams with sparse reuse. Jonah — can you share args?
jonah: Synthetic runner snippet (staging):
```
./kv_loadgen --tenants alpha-payments --sessions 200 --avg_len 1800 --prefix_repeat_rate 0.06 --interarrival=0.8s --duration=45m
```
This produces the same rising residency pattern on my staging rack.
deploy-bot: Canary runtime-v3.8.2 started @ 2198769000 (changeset: adjust eviction scoring + soft tenant watermark).
alex_m: For rollout plan: 1) add telemetry: per-tenant residency histogram + per-tenant eviction_age distribution; 2) enable scoring change behind feature-flag; 3) ramp to 10% tenants; 4) observe pagerate/latency.
matthew: Perf check — scoring change increases compute in eviction path (extra math), but it's O(1) per candidate. Batching heuristics change could be triggered if we change when we compact; watch p99 CPU of runtime threads.
priya_r: Also record a reuse decay metric so we don't punish tenants with bursty reuse. Something like reuse_decay_window=5m.
jonah: I ran the staging runner against v3.8.2 FF-on: residency plateaued (instead of climbing): p50 token latency improved 210ms -> 135ms, eviction rate down 12/s -> 4/s. Breaking numbers: kv_residency_ratio=0.55, kv_evictions_total=132, avg_kv_reuse=0.18.
ingrid: Nice. Any regressions observed elsewhere?
jonah: Ran a smoke across small-head models: negligible CPU overhead, p99 CPU +1.3% on eviction threads under synthetic load. No impact on unrelated tenants in staging.
alex_m: Next actions:
- instrument tenant heatmaps + add alert: tenant residency growth > 15% in 15m -> paging-surge alert
- promote scoring FF to 20% ring tomorrow if canary stays green
- add a background compaction pass that prefers pages with low reuse_count and high age
- add docs for ops to set tenant soft_quota overrides
priya_r: I'll own the alert + dashboards. matthew, can you add the scoring code as a small patch so we can review?
matthew: On it, sending PR with tests for scoring edgecases.
jonah: TL;DR — root cause likely interplay between batching tweak and long-context sparse reuse causing KV churn. Mitigate with eviction scoring & soft per-tenant watermarks; staging results look promising. Will post PR & staging graphs in #eng-runtime after lunch. :thumbsup:
ingrid: Great summary. Add an A/B note so we can measure user-visible SLOs vs internal token latencies.
jonah: Will do. Thanks all.
